purpose: Select one coherent Debian Trixie release base and produce the complete immutable graph from which one AUZiX base generation is built.

upstream_model.authority: Debian source packages, Debian patches, Debian build metadata, and Debian dependency/provider decisions from the selected snapshot
upstream_model.selection_rule: All selected sources, binaries, build dependencies, runtime dependencies, and virtual providers must resolve inside the same immutable snapshot. Ambient apt candidates are forbidden after discovery.

base_model.rule: One snapshot produces one AUZiX base generation. Every package in that generation is built against the same selected base.
protected_components: DBus, PAM, udev and service substrate
X11, EFL and Enlightenment desktop substrate
base_model.leaf_rule: A leaf package consumes the selected base ABI and cannot redefine or upgrade it.
base_model.base_transition_rule: A requirement for a newer protected component rejects the leaf transaction and requires a new complete base-generation plan.

discovery_inputs: Debian source package debian/control and generated package metadata
AUZiX filesystem and lifecycle translation policy
required_lock_outputs: snapshot identity and repository metadata digests
complete selected binary and source package totals
exact versions, architectures, source URLs and checksums
protected base ABI and symbol floors
Git commit and proposed immutable tag
hard_failures: multiple selected providers for a protected component
selected binary requires a symbol newer than the selected base
source cannot build against the selected base
package or dependency appears after the lock
compile or root mutation begins during discovery

build_handoff.rule: The build consumes only the reviewed lock and exact Git tag.
order: freeze and identify the AUZiX native builder
build remaining libraries and applications against that builder
package with translated Debian lifecycle semantics
validate in a fresh root as root and normal user
assemble images only from validated packages

terminal_condition: Stop after producing a finite, reviewable, checksummed lock. Do not compile in the discovery run.
